subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: For provider routes that emit a bare visible marker like `[tool: exec]` with no arguments and no structured tool call, should OpenClaw warn/block, retry/fail over, force or shrink the tool surface, or attempt a new recovery format?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the correct response changes runtime/provider policy and directly executing the reported marker is not safe because it lacks arguments.

options.title: Warn and fail over before execution
options.body: Detect bare markers, avoid executing them, surface a diagnostic, and either retry or move to a tool-capable fallback with tests for provider and embedded-runner paths.

options.title: Add model-specific formatting or tool-surface limits
options.body: Keep the current parser boundary and reduce the likelihood of bare markers by changing prompts, tool schema size, or provider capability gating for affected models.

options.title: Define a new recoverable marker contract
options.body: Teach the repair layer a supported bracket format only if maintainers define how arguments are supplied and how unsafe or ambiguous markers are rejected.

recommendation.title: Warn and fail over before execution
recommendation.body: Detect bare markers, avoid executing them, surface a diagnostic, and either retry or move to a tool-capable fallback with tests for provider and embedded-runner paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to the provider stream, diagnostics, and SDK-boundary decisions that the policy choice would affect.
